system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The Planner is given the context of tools present in the system, the stages that have already completed, the current stage and the future stages, along with the original user prompt.
system_prompt_style.note: Per-agent system prompts composed from stage context, tool lists and prior execution results; paper-only.

env_context_strategy.note: Paper-only; no repository/environment context mechanism described. Value set to null per not_reported.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: After each stage, theExecution Agentreflects on the tool outputs and summarizes, keeping only the relevant information to be passed as context to the next stage.

observation_format.evidence_quote: returns clean text content for that web page
observation_format.note: MCP tool outputs as text; paper-only.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: a set of available functions, defined as JSON schema objects within the tools parameter

tool_count.note: Tools come from MCP servers per application; no default built-in tool list.

edit_primitive.note: No code/tool registry available; paper only.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: The Stage agent also has the list of MCP tools descriptions from the MCP server or even the Doc String of a Python function as possible actions.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: We focus mainly on the MCP protocol for integrating our agents with external sources and evaluating them, and leave A2A as future work.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the stage agent breaks down the task into a set of high level objectives called stages; the planner and the execution agents then processes each stage sequentially.
loop_primitives.note: Executor loops tool calls and reflection (react) within each stage.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: AgentX employs a two-tier hierarchy where theStage Generation Agentfirst creates a high-level, coarse grained plan (stages), and then thePlanner Agent creates a detailed, fine grained plan for each stage.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: composed of stage designer, planner, and executor agents
multi_agent_topology.note: Fixed hand-off Stage -> Planner -> Executor per stage.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The execution agent also generates execution results after each stage that is passed on as context for the next stage.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: These results are later saved in a local variable which is used to provide context to the first phase of the execution agent.
short_term_state.note: Stages list, plan, execution results with success flag via pydantic structured outputs.

self_verification.evidence_quote: the execution agent is passed two attributes in its output schema: theexecution resultsand aflagto denote if the plan has successfully executed or not.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: In its current form, AgentX lacks a dedicated recovery system.
retry_policy.note: Executor retries tool calls within a stage (step-level), not task-level.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The user's task is completed when all the stages provided by the Stage Generation agent are completed successfully.

cost_controls.note: Tool filtering reduces tokens but no budget/caching mechanism described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: we deploy the MCP servers on AWS Lambda using the distributed approach
execution_isolation.note: Both local MCP servers (subprocess) and FaaS evaluated; no default stated.

permission_model.note: Planner tool filtering is not authorisation.

tracing.note: Paper says 'The execution trace is returned by each module' without format.

eval_hooks.note: No repo; LLM-judge scoring used in experiments.

target_domain.evidence_quote: designed to execute a generalized execution flow applicable to any application defined by a user prompt.

model_agnostic.note: Only gpt-4o-mini via openai library evaluated.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: We implement our AgentX pattern using a Python framework consisting of modules for the different agent types and an orchestrator between the agents to implement the interaction pattern.
